review_scope: Independent method, feature, selection, and score review for prospective real iFlex factual prediction comparison; no fit or outcome read
principal_conclusion: The proposed same-data predictive comparison is scientifically appropriate if reported as factual load/energy forecasting for already observed households on later dates. Four discrete price intensities do not support use or field validation of the current pure-continuous DR curve.
source: work/b1_real_response_data_20261103/prepared_P_events.csv, metadata ID/Group/Region/Date/split/signal/level and readiness flags only

metadata_support.support_interpretation: Train contains all 12 group-by-level cells and all 718 households appearing later. Neither later split introduces a new group-level cell. Validation did not assess level15; test does not assess level5; all718 level15 test records share one date. Keep frozen split and report scope, do not reshuffle to fill holes. Level-specific dates can overlap, so do not sum their counts as independent dates.

pre_fit_requirements: Explicitly set early_stopping=False for both HGB variants and lock max_iter within the four permitted settings. Local sklearn1.7.2 source enables default auto early stopping only above10000 samples: 9581 training rows versus11794 after train+validation would otherwise silently change the refit policy and introduce a random internal holdout.

Freeze exact feature allowlist. Source-approved pre-notice 24h/168h consumption and 24h temperature, group/region and calendar variables known at notice are eligible. Do not use same-day realized weather, current outcomes, source row IDs, splits, post-treatment survey, reward or price-dependent outcome proxies. Household ID is a grouping key unless an explicitly declared known-user predictor is part of every applicable control.

Price-free controls must omit assigned_signal, nominal_price_level, the 24h price path, deterministic transforms of these, and all price interactions. Group/region/calendar can remain common pre-notice state; they do not make this a randomized feature ablation or causal effect.

Fit encoders, centering and scaling using training rows only for validation. Once hyperparameters are frozen, refit the exact same pipeline on train+validation and transform test without estimating any feature statistic on test.

Reuse the old auxiliary outcome-model structure only: polynomial degree2 pretreatment features, six-knot cubic amount basis, X-by-basis interactions, Ridge. Refit on real outcome kWh and use the real discrete 2..15 NOK/kWh domain. It is not the old full Kennedy DR estimator, its fitted simulated weights, GPS, or an identified continuous causal curve.

At four actually observed price levels, a seven-column spline basis has rank at most4 on amount rows. Ridge can regularize redundant columns, but no intermediate-price or derivative accuracy is tested. Linear-price control may preserve comparable X-by-price interactions if the goal is isolate price basis shape; if only additive, call it a distinct operational baseline, not a pure basis ablation.

Make HGB-price consume the same expanded price/state features as spline-Ridge. Make HGB-no-price use the matching state design after removing all price columns/interactions. Give each its same four candidate budget; compare both on exact same test roster.

Prespecify whether the secondary 24h outcome independently receives the same fixed four validation choices per method or reuses the main outcome's selected settings. Do not choose between these rules after viewing validation or test outcomes.

Select each method once using only frozen whole-date validation primary score, with fixed tie rule. Preserve all validation candidates and the chosen config/source hash. Refit each fixed model exactly once on train+validation, open fixed test once, and retain every prediction/score even if the candidate loses.

Historical load features may contain earlier treated days and earlier evaluation dates' observations that genuinely precede a later event notice. This is valid for sequential forecasting with observed current history; it is not an untreated baseline or a single multi-day forecast from the first origin. No leakage if no later observations or realized current-event values enter an earlier prediction.

score_contract.primary_peak: For each complete test date d compute sqrt(sum_i[(y_id-pred_id)^2]/n_d) in kWh, then take arithmetic mean over the five dates. Same roster for all methods. Do not replace by sqrt(mean of date MSE) or pooled RMSE.
score_contract.secondary: 24h measured consumption kWh; pooled individual RMSE and MAE; per-date error table; group-day mean calibration using separate errors of observed and predicted within-group means, with group-day count and date dependence stated.
score_contract.coverage: Report outcomes and prediction availability using 2419 designed events and five whole test dates, with group-day count10 and actual tested levels 2/10/15. Do not improve scores by method-specific row deletion.
score_contract.uncertainty: Only five later dates and repeated known households. Paired per-date differences or leave-one-date descriptive sensitivity are useful, but row-level bootstrap/row-level statistical significance would exaggerate independent evidence.
score_contract.price_increment: Price-HGB vs no-price-HGB and price-Ridge vs history-Ridge quantify incremental predictive usefulness under the observed schedule. An improvement is not a causal price effect; no improvement does not prove price has no effect. Never turn RMSE into causal accuracy percentage.

verified_code_sources.finding: Old auxiliary design is X, amount basis B, and X-by-B interaction columns; the Kennedy DR pseudo-outcome and density fit are separate.
Old auxiliary predictor uses degree2 polynomial X, training scaler, cubic fixed-knot SplineTransformer and Ridge.
Inspected installed official code: early_stopping auto is n_samples>10000. Must explicitly disable for fixed-budget comparison.

limits_to_report: Real measured household kWh, not EV effective-response duration
Known-household future-date generalization, not new household generalization
No untreated counterfactual truth, causal effect curve RMSE, derivative accuracy, or continuous-price deployment claim
Model design review only; actual implementation and resulting scores require independent audit
